rationale: No candidate supplies the child's distinctive Section 123 machinery: submission of a proposed atomic-cooperation agreement to the Joint Committee, findings concerning common defense and unreasonable risk, approval of the agreement, authorization of its execution, and delegation to communicate Restricted Data. C25 and C09 are the closest in using statutory notification letters followed by presidential determinations, while C15 authorizes interagency support for an international organization, but these are generic parallels under different statutes and do not reproduce a concrete, material drafting sequence from the child.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Pursuant to Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, I hereby submit to the Joint Committee on Atomic Energy a proposed agreement
shared_material.parent_excerpt: In compliance with Section 101(a)(1) of the Mutual Security Act of 1951, I hereby notify you that I have today determined
shared_material.explanation: C25 shares a statute-triggered congressional notification and determination formula, but not the atomic-agreement approval and Restricted Data machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Accordingly, I hereby determine that its performance will promote and will not constitute an unreasonable risk to the common defense and security
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have therefore determined, pursuant to the provisions of Section 101(b) of the Mutual Security Act of 1951
shared_material.explanation: C09 uses a similar presidential statutory-determination form, but the operative subject is a transfer of appropriations rather than approval of an international atomic-information agreement.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Department of Defense, with the assistance of the Atomic Energy Commission, to cooperate with the North Atlantic Treaty Organization and to communicate Restricted Data
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Secretary of State...is authorized...to request the Secretary of Defense to detail personnel...and to furnish facilities, services, or other assistance...to the United Nations
shared_material.explanation: C15 has interagency authority to assist an international organization, but its personnel-and-services framework is materially different and contains none of the child's agreement, safeguards, findings, or Restricted Data provisions.
